beats.care: El Niño often means weaker monsoons and hotter weather in India, which can push up food prices and strain water supplies.
beats.what: The World Meteorological Organization says the current El Niño will strengthen and peak around December, possibly among the strongest since 1950.
beats.why: Forecasters expect the central Pacific to run about 3.7 degrees above normal, beating the record set in 2015 and 2016.

cards.body: Thirteen global forecasting centres agree El Niño will almost surely last through February 2027. The last record, in 2015–16, was about 2.6°C above normal.

cards.note: Sea-surface temperature above normal in the central Pacific.
cards.title: Pacific warming in big El Niño years

cards.body: In an El Niño, warm water shifts east across the Pacific. That changes winds worldwide and often weakens the moist winds that bring India its rain.
cards.title: how does the pacific affect our monsoon?

cards.body: El Niño is Spanish for 'the boy child'. Fishermen in Peru named it centuries ago because warm water often arrived near Christmas.
